findings.what: routes.ts: RouteLevel.obj is now `Node` and stands for the runtime route object. wrapperLevels(mount, call, path, auxAt) passes the call expression to levelOf as the identity, so two calls of a wrapper are two levels. A route literal referenced by name keeps the literal as its identity, so it is still shared. Three call sites are affected: the element call, the spread call, and `children: wrapper(...)`. One case is not keyed per call: an array-returning builder such as `section(X)` returning `[{path, children}]`. The reader cannot place a parameter-filled subtree under such a builder (it declares the subtree unread), so two calls cannot produce distinct screens there.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a route a wrapper builds > gives each call of a wrapper its own route object, and shares it within one call': /home->/about is may with guard auth; /home->/near (same call) stays must

findings.what: Each level records `consumes` (how many segments its own path has) and `matrix` (runGuardsAndResolvers is unset or 'paramsChange'). runningGuards(from, to, preserved, tried) stops keeping levels at the first level that is matrix-sensitive and whose cumulative consumed segments exceed `preserved`; the count is cumulative because Angular's check recurses through parents. emitTargets computes preserved = keptSegments(parsed.path, base): the source route's segment count minus its leading '..'. It is used only for relative commands with a known base that did not go through a redirect. land() now returns `redirected`. Absolute commands, URLs and controls mode use 0. 'pathParamsChange' behaves as before. guards-run.test.ts:46 now expects may with guard auth for the absolute link /app/one->/app/two.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'runs a canActivate the navigation enters, and a shared route's again where an absolute link drops its matrix parameters' (changed expectation) and 'matrix parameters ... keeps a shared route a relative link does not climb out of, and runs it again on one that does': ../two stays must; ../../app/two is may/auth; a 'pathParamsChange' parent with an absolute link stays must

findings.what: The redirects map is now Map<string, Redirect> with {to, prefix, levels}, and prefix is set unless pathMatch === 'full'. extract.ts redirectsAt(path, id) uses the new overlaps() in matcher.ts. A redirect is a rival when it is declared at a ':' pattern that matches the address, or when it is a prefix redirect at a shorter address; catch-alls are excluded. land() counts every rival toward ambiguity, and hidden() uses the same test. Without one more rule this lost two correct mifos must edges: /centers/create and /groups/create would be shadowed by a ':centerId' or ':groupId' redirect declared after them. So a redirect is not a rival when the screen's branch and the redirect's branch split at sibling objects of one array literal and the screen comes first. Every other ordering is treated as unknown and the redirect stays a rival.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'redirects the router meets before the screen ...': /old/x, /item/new and /gone/new are may; /z/y (full-path redirect at z) and /q/new (declared before q/:id) stay must

findings.what: levelOf records every non-aux level that has canMatch or canLoad, and every guarded aux level, into a per-collectRoutes `guardedLevels` list, which collectRoutes exposes through its new `guarded` out-parameter. Probe walks are excluded. land() collects into `tried` every guarded level whose path prefix-overlaps any address on the way, including the addresses before each redirect hop. runningGuards then adds canMatch and canLoad for tried levels that are not on the target's chain, deduplicated by obj. This is a sound over-approximation: declaration order is ignored.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'canMatch on the routes the router tries on the way ...': /a->/b is may with adminOnly from an earlier '' route; /a->/beta->/new is may with beta from the branch the redirect passes through

findings.what: A route that has a redirectTo property is now registered even when stringProp cannot read it. It gets {to: null}, and a host's redirectsTo becomes null. hidden() is true for such a host. When land() meets a null target it stops and marks the landing ambiguous, and a sibling unreadable redirect counts as a rival. Unreadable redirects still do not count toward `placed`, so the unplaced-file accounting is unchanged; an existing regression test pins this.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a redirect whose target the reader cannot fix ...': /a->/p (empty-path child redirectTo: () => 'c') is may; /a->/x (sibling redirectTo: () => '/a') is may; /p->/a is may because /p is hidden

findings.what: level.resolve is now also true when titleResolves(obj). A title is static when stringProp reads it, or when stringValued() finds a string, template, tagged template ($localize) or null literal, following names and properties to their initializers. Otherwise the type checker decides: a type with call or construct signatures is a resolver, and a type made only of string-like or null members is static. Anything unreadable is treated as a resolver. ghostfolio's internalRoutes.x.title chains still read as static.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'a title resolver ...': title as an arrow function and title as a class are may; TITLES.b ($localize) and the string 'Lit' stay must

findings.what: Chosen fix: demotion, the sound option. walkElements threads `auxAt`, the address where the outermost named-outlet route is mounted (it replaces the underAuxOutlet boolean), and aux levels record it. runningGuards adds an aux level's canDeactivate whenever the source path lies under its mount, and an empty-path aux level's canMatch, canActivate, canActivateChild and canLoad (and its resolve) whenever the target lies under its mount. It does not tell apart navigations that keep the outlet open, so it over-demotes in apps that have guarded aux routes. The corpus has none.
findings.test: guards-run.test.ts 'routes on a named outlet ...': /a->/ and navigateByUrl('/b') are may with leave (root popup canDeactivate); /a->/c carries gate from the empty-path 'side' outlet route

report.thesisProseToChange:
- thesis-handoff/thesis/ch3-analysis.tex:152-154 ("The routes the source and the target share are reused unless their parameters can change or runGuardsAndResolvers asks otherwise"): under the default mode a shared route is now also rerun when the navigation can drop a matrix parameter of a segment it or a parent consumes (an absolute link, a URL, a redirected landing, or a relative link climbing above it). "Share" now means the same runtime object, and each wrapper call is its own object.
- ch3-analysis.tex:154-155 ("A navigation runs the canMatch of every route its address is matched through"): it now also counts canMatch and canLoad of every route the router may try at an address on the way, including abandoned earlier routes and branches a redirect passes through.
- ch3-analysis.tex:160-161 ("A resolver is awaited by the router and demotes the edge"): still true, but it now covers a title that is not a string.
- ch3-analysis.tex:167-169 (demoted "when the address is one that two declared routes, or a route and a redirect, can answer"): prefix and parameter-pattern redirects and unreadable redirectTo now count. A screen declared before a redirect in the same table is not demoted by it.
- ch3-analysis.tex:170 ("when a URL names an auxiliary outlet, whose route the adapter does not read"): the adapter now reads guarded named-outlet routes. Their canDeactivate counts for sources under their mount, and an empty-path one's guards count for targets under it.
- ch5-results.tex:1042-1046 ("canMatch on every level it matches ... a level is kept when source and destination pass through the same route object, the level has no parameter the navigation could change, and it does not ask to run its guards on every navigation"): the kept rule gains the matrix condition (the navigation must keep every segment consumed up to that level unless the mode is 'pathParamsChange'), and canMatch also runs on tried routes.
- ch6-discussion.tex:607 (canMatch "of a route its address is matched through"): same change as ch3:154-155.
- ch6-discussion.tex:610-612 ("A route the source and target share is taken to be reused unless its path has a parameter or runGuardsAndResolvers is set, which a parameter that does not in fact change makes too cautious"): the rule now also requires the navigation to keep the consumed segments, so this description of the rule is wrong.
- ch6-discussion.tex:626-628 ("consults a redirect only when no route matches. Wherever two declared routes, or a route and a redirect, can answer an address, the edge is held at may"): declaration order is now read for a screen and a redirect that are siblings in one table; the screen declared first is not held at may on that redirect's account. Prefix and parameter redirects now count as rivals.
- No count sentence (CensusMust, GuardOnlyMust, the per-app must figures) becomes false. Figures built from may or total edge counts or from edge ids would shift as described in corpusImpact.

problems.what: The aux-outlet model still misses guards that a named-outlet route runs while it stays open. For an outlet the source may have open, runningGuards adds only canDeactivate. But recognition re-runs that route's canMatch on every navigation, and runGuardsAndResolvers 'always' re-runs its canActivate and resolvers. An absolute routerLink keeps the root's other outlets, so those guards run and the must edge is unsound (Claim 3.1). This is not a regression (main is also must), but the commit already collects these levels (auxLevels) and then drops the canMatch. The fix is one line: add ...l.canMatch to closing, plus canActivate and resolve when l.always.
problems.evidence: Fixture: routes [{path:'a',component:A},{path:'b',component:P},{path:'compose',component:P,outlet:'popup',canMatch:[cm]}], A has <a routerLink="/b">. Worktree gives /a->/b must guard=null. The same fixture with canActivate:[g], runGuardsAndResolvers:'always' on the popup route instead also gives must, on both main and the worktree. Angular 21.2.12 (_router-chunk.mjs): an absolute command gets Position(root, processChildren=true) at :781-783. updateSegmentGroupChildren then copies every other root outlet at :856-860, so /a(popup:compose) becomes /b(popup:compose). matchWithChecks at :2779-2788 runs runCanMatchGuards on every route that recognize matches, with no reuse check.

problems.what: Precision regression from main. overlaps() treats a ':' on the address side as a wildcard, and hidden() feeds it a screen's route pattern. So a literal redirect that covers one instance of a parameterised screen marks the whole screen as never displayed, and every edge from it drops to may. This is sound but loses correct must edges. hidden() should need the redirect pattern to cover the screen pattern, not just one instance of it.
problems.evidence: Fixture: [{path:'items/new',redirectTo:'/a',pathMatch:'full'},{path:'items/:id',component:P},{path:'a',component:A}], P has <a routerLink="/a">. The edge /items/:id -> /a is must on main and may (guard null) on the worktree. /items/5 still shows P, so the must edge was correct.

problems.what: Four of the new demotion sub-rules have no test that fails when the rule is removed: (1) cumulative consumed, (2) preserved forced to 0 after a redirect (!landed.redirected), (3) collecting tried at hops after the first, (4) the later prefix redirect upgrading an earlier full one (Object.assign(first,{prefix,levels:[]})). Each mutant survives the full adapter suite. The repo's practice is to kill uncovered demotion rules (a014ac2).
problems.evidence: I ran each mutant in a scratch copy: consumed = l.consumes; dropping && !landed.redirected; if (hop === 0) tried.push(...); deleting the routes.ts:991 branch. The suite stayed at the unmutated baseline every time (13 environment-only golden failures from the copy's missing examples/ path, 344 passing), so no test catches any of the four. Rule (1) does matter. Fixture: {path:'x',runGuardsAndResolvers:'pathParamsChange',children:[{path:'',component:P,canActivate:[auth],children:[one,two]}]}, with an absolute /x/two from /x/one. It gives may with auth; the non-cumulative mutant would give must.

problems.what: The justification is false: Angular does not match '**' last. match() takes '**' in declaration order like any other route. The exclusion is an unstated assumption, and 126 of the corpus's 150 must edges depend on it. k8sdash's '**' is in a different root table from its screens. The router puts it after them only because ChromeModule is imported before RouterModule.forRoot, and the walk does not read import order. Not a regression (main assumed the same implicitly). It should be stated as a soundiness assumption, or checked with before() when the catch-all shares an array with the screen.
problems.evidence: Fixture: {path:'adm',children:[{path:'**',redirectTo:'/a'},{path:'x',component:P}]} gives /a->/adm/x must, but Angular redirects /adm/x to /a. With the !at.endsWith('*') guard removed, corpus must edges go k8sdash 125->0 and bitwarden 1->0. Sources: k8sdash src/index.routing.ts ([login, '' redirect, '**' redirect]), src/chrome/routing.ts (forChild screens), src/index.module.ts:33-35 (ChromeModule imported before forRoot).

problems.what: The fix-4 claim that 'the unplaced-file accounting is unchanged' is inaccurate. Probe walks now register redirects with a null target, so a claimed but unwalked file whose only route is a function-valued redirectTo is now declared unplaced. That adds an incomplete-route-set note, which voids dead-link claims across the whole app. The new behaviour is the safe direction, but it is undisclosed and untested.

The link then goes down the catch-all branch: it gets a may edge to the catch-all screen and a note that it matches no declared route.
